tagline: Up Alameda Creek beside the first transcontinental line.
intro: From the Niles district of Fremont, Niles Canyon Road follows the canyon Alameda Creek cut, about seven miles up to Sunol. Two railroads keep it company, the old Southern Pacific on the north side and the Union Pacific a little to the south. At the canyon's west end stand the ruins of the Vallejo Flour Mill, which dates to 1853.

The Southern Pacific track was the westernmost piece of the first transcontinental railroad, and the first through train from Sacramento came down this canyon in September 1869. Ten years later the through traffic went to a shorter route by way of Benicia, and around 1900 Niles became a destination for picnic day-trippers.

moments.title: Niles
moments.text: Essanay made more than 350 films here between 1912 and 1916, and Charlie Chaplin shot The Tramp in the canyon before the chilly weather sent him south.

moments.title: Niles Canyon Railway
moments.text: Steam and diesel excursions run between Sunol and Niles on track that Chinese laborers graded into the canyon's tight curves in the 1860s.

moments.title: Sunol
moments.text: The town got its post office in 1871 and, the same year, the name Sunolglen, which it kept until 1920, when it went back to plain Sunol.
